where: Section 2, first two sentences of the GPRS paragraph
problem: The phrase 'are an order of 100 kbps' and 'at an order of' is awkward English and can confuse readers whose first language is not English; the standard phrase is 'of the order of'.
fix: GPRS data rates are of the order of 100 kbps; the common textbook peak is 171.2 kbps. EDGE improved the modulation and reached rates of the order of 200 kbps.

problem: 'They do not replace the air interface' can be read as 'the radio interface does not change at all', which is wrong: EDGE changes the modulation to 8-PSK and HSDPA adds a new shared downlink channel with 16-QAM. The true point is that no new generation of radio interface is introduced.
fix: 2.5G and 3.5G are upgrades inside the same system. GPRS, EDGE and HSDPA add new channels and modulation to the existing GSM or WCDMA air interface; they do not introduce a new generation of radio interface.

problem: 'about 1 ms in the radio link' does not say which direction or which plane, so a student cannot tell what the 1 ms measures.
fix: It also targets low latency: about 1 ms one-way user-plane latency over the radio link for some services.

problem: AMPS is a frequency-division duplex system, so a call holds one uplink frequency and one downlink frequency, not a single frequency channel. The simplification can mislead about how the channel is used.
fix: Each call took one channel pair: one frequency for the uplink and one for the downlink.

problem: 'The internal GSM, GPRS and UMTS architecture' is vague; 'internal' does not tell the student what is in Chapter 1.3.
fix: The network architecture of GSM, GPRS and UMTS is covered in Chapter 1.3.

problem: The unit is written '40,000,000 bit' (singular) while the quantity is many bits; this is a small unit-writing slip in a chapter that asks students to be careful with units.
